notes_for_editor: Roster: the USLHS place record puts Ka Lae at 18.0931, -155.6842 (about 91 km from the station's record position, 18.91218, -155.681855); the roster was matched by name, the only Ka Lae place in the archive. Check that the place page is the right light before accepting its keeper list. The keepers are the archive's NARA-register reading; no primary keeper register was checked. Lighthouse Board reports for 1905-1910 are not in the local corpus (the corpus has the Board's reports only to 1901); the 1906 first lighting and 1907-08 events rest on LighthouseFriends, which prints Otwell's 1907 report, and on the 1907 Hawaiian Gazette. The 1906/1909 disagreement is unresolved. The steel tower year (1928 or 1929) is unresolved. The Bulletin 1921 and 1930 pages are two-column scans; the evidence quotes are copied from the OCR as it stands, errors included, and some are short fragments because the columns interleave. The 1921 keeper's letter is known only through the Bulletin summary and LighthouseFriends' print of it. Wikipedia was used only for leads; its NRHP and NHL dates are not used. No NHL date is given in the story because no source was read for it. The 'Swedish Space Corporation' dish is from LighthouseFriends and may have changed. Ranges: the sources give 'nine miles' for the 1906 lantern without saying whether nautical; the guide asks for nautical miles, so confirm before publication. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the story was checked sentence by sentence against LighthouseFriends (cite 2), the Bulletin pages (PDF p. 5 and p. 6), the Hawaiian Gazette page and Rowlett (cite 1). LighthouseFriends gives the same ten head keepers and years as the USLHS roster (cite 6), so the keeper list is corroborated by two sources; the USLHS place record behind the roster was matched by name and sits about 91 km from the station, so a human should still confirm that the place page is this light. The 1907 dwelling is recorded as other because the Gazette reports a plan, not a completion. Rowlett gives 1909 for establishment and 1929 for the steel tower; LighthouseFriends gives 1928 for the tower, and both are stated in the story. Rowlett also calls the area a National Historic Landmark with no date; that is now in Today. The 1921 Bulletin prints the gale as north middle-dot northeast (OCR); the story writes north-northeast. Nine sentences that followed LighthouseFriends or Rowlett wording too closely were rewritten. Miles for the lantern range and Otwell's ten miles are kept as miles because no source says nautical.
